company.name: Linear
company.oneLiner: Linear sells issue tracking and product planning software for software teams, with built-in agents and automation.
company.customers: Product and engineering teams, from free workspaces to enterprises; the site names OpenAI and Ramp and says it powers over 50,000 product teams.

blueprint.headline: Linear sells intake, triage, and agents to product teams; its own agents should run sales and support on that same platform, so each internal workflow becomes a reference customers can copy.

agents.name: Enterprise Security Review Drafter
agents.role: Drafts answers to security questionnaires for Enterprise deals from approved answers and the plan's documented controls.
agents.trigger: When a sales opportunity attaches a security questionnaire
does: Maps each question to an approved answer covering SAML and SCIM, audit log, HIPAA compliance, and the uptime SLA
Marks questions with no approved answer instead of improvising one
Fills the buyer's format and attaches the draft to the opportunity

humanGate.detail: Nothing goes to a buyer until the security team signs off. Any answer marked as new or changed needs the security lead.

agents.evidence: The Enterprise plan is sold through Contact sales and is defined by controls buyers audit: SAML and SCIM, audit log, HIPAA compliance, granular admin controls, and an uptime SLA.
agents.impact: Enterprise deals stop waiting on the security team to retype the same answers, and every claim sent to a buyer comes from an approved source.

agents.name: Support Request Linker
agents.role: Connects each support conversation to the matching customer request and existing issue, so product sees demand with the account attached.
agents.trigger: When a conversation arrives through Zendesk, Intercom, Slack intake, or email intake
does: Finds the existing issue or customer request that matches the conversation
Attaches the account and plan to that customer request, or proposes a new one
Drafts the reply telling the customer whether the item is planned, in progress, or not yet scheduled

humanGate.detail: Links to existing requests apply automatically because they are reversible. Every customer reply, and any statement about timing, is sent by a support engineer.

agents.evidence: The site sells Customer requests, Slack and email intake, and Zendesk and Intercom integrations, the same intake path its own support would use.
agents.impact: Prioritization reflects which accounts asked for what, and customers get accurate status replies without support digging through the backlog.

agents.name: Changelog Drafter
agents.role: Drafts changelog entries from what actually shipped in each release.
agents.trigger: When a release is marked complete in Releases
does: Reads the issues and merged pull requests in the release
Groups user-facing changes and drops internal-only work
Drafts entries in the existing changelog voice, noting which plans each feature is on

humanGate.detail: Drafts only. An editor approves and publishes every changelog entry; plan availability is checked by product marketing.

agents.evidence: The site publishes a Changelog, ships features tiered across Free, Basic, Business, and Enterprise, and offers Releases and a GitHub integration.
agents.impact: The changelog keeps pace with shipping, and plan availability is stated correctly in every entry.

agents.name: Business Plan Fit Scout
agents.role: Finds workspaces whose usage matches the problems Business plan features solve and briefs the account owner.
does: Reads workspace usage for teams on Free and Basic
Matches patterns such as heavy triage load or many requests arriving from Slack to Business features like Triage Intelligence, Slack intake, and Issue SLAs
Writes a short internal brief per account with the evidence

humanGate.detail: It writes internal notes only. Any outreach to the customer is written and sent by a person.

agents.evidence: The pricing page separates plans by concrete features: Triage on Free, while Triage Intelligence, Insights, Linear Asks, Issue SLAs, and Slack intake are Business features.
agents.impact: Upgrade conversations start from the customer's real workflow instead of a seat count.

firstBuild.why: Linking is reversible, replies are already reviewed by support, and it runs on Linear's own Customer requests, so it is a reference implementation from day one.
scope: Ingest Zendesk and Intercom conversations through the existing integrations
Propose a link to an existing customer request with a confidence note
Auto-apply links above a reviewed confidence threshold; queue the rest for support
Draft status replies for support to send

blueprint.nonObvious: Linear's best sales asset for its agent platform is its own operations. If its support, security reviews, and changelog run on Linear Agent, Loops, and Customer requests, each internal agent becomes a working template for the 50,000 teams the site mentions, and any rough edge is found by Linear before a customer finds it.
caveats: Curated by hand from the public site, not produced by a live run.
Linear's internal sales, support, and analytics tools are not visible; CRM and analytics are named by category.
Assumed Linear's own support uses the Zendesk and Intercom paths it sells; the site does not say so.
